PullRequest.Title: Title bar: Keep menus above workbench content
PullRequest.Body:

This keeps application menus above Explorer and editor content when the title bar is inactive.

### Changes

- Keep inactive title bars dimmed until the application menubar is focused or open.
- Restore full title-bar container opacity while the menubar is active, avoiding the stacking context that trapped menus beneath sibling workbench parts.
- Clear menubar focus styling when the custom menubar is removed.
- Add regression coverage for inactive and focused menubar opacity.

Fixes #340237

### Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.test.ts` — 5 passing
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.ts src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.test.ts` — passed
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/media/titlebarpart.css` — passed with six pre-existing design-token suggestions
- Windows-emulated web workbench — confirmed the menu paints above Explorer and editor content, while inactive opacity returns after closing it

Scenarios.Scenario: Install the custom application menubar during workbench/title-bar creation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Title-bar creation instantiates the existing CustomMenubarControl and creates its DOM; the diff adds one in-process event subscription before creation. No asynchronous or external work must complete because of the new code.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One listener per BrowserTitlebarPart/custom menubar instance; cardinality is constant rather than proportional to menu items, editors, or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous setup on the UI thread with no queue, parallelism, or fan-out introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache reads, misses, keys, invalidation, or coalescing are involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed setup line and emitter ownership are directly traced, and the disposable store removes the listener on uninstall.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style-engine costs vary, but installation adds only a dormant listener and no style change until focus changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: constant listener setup has negligible cost and correct bounded cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Focus, open, and close the application menubar while the window/title bar is inactive
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing MenuBar focus-state transition synchronously emits a boolean; the new listener toggles one class, and CSS updates opacity for the fixed-size title-bar container. This is on the interaction path, but only on transitions into or out of focused/open state, not per menu item, frame, or pointer movement.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One class mutation and one title-bar style/compositing update per focus-state transition; work is independent of workspace size and menu action count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-thread event handling; no burst, loop, or unbounded scheduling is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved; normal browser selector/style caching may apply equally across repeated transitions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: MenuBar suppresses identical focus states and fires only after state changes; the added callback performs a single classList.toggle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact repaint/compositor behavior depends on browser and platform, but the affected region is the bounded title bar and transition frequency is user-driven and low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the bounded style invalidation is necessary for the intended visual/stacking behavior and does not scale with realistic collection size or run at frame frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remove or reinstall the custom menubar after menu-bar visibility configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Uninstall clears the existing disposable stores and menubar, then the diff synchronously removes the focus class before removing the menubar DOM. No external operation blocks progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per infrequent configuration-driven uninstall; one listener and one class token are cleaned up.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized synchronous configuration handling on the UI thread; no concurrency or pending work is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the listener is registered in customMenubarDisposables, cleared before control disposal, and the class is explicitly removed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration changes are user-driven and rare; there is no meaningful scale uncertainty.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: cleanup prevents retained listeners/stale styling and adds only constant DOM work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced the new focus-state listener through CustomMenubarControl and MenuBar. The diff adds bounded UI-thread class/style work only on menubar focus transitions, with explicit disposal on uninstall and no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, serialization, cache, collection fan-out, or concurrency changes. No actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
